title: Ghostbusters II
uncounted: the RAM under the I/O area holds data, and game.json does not say what it is (kit/skills/c64/c64-reference, "RAM the CPU cannot see")

records.c: Call the interrupt helper, set border and background black, select video bank 1 and VIC memory and display settings, increment $0E, then call the helper at $1907 with X=$05, Y=$18 and A=$7A before jumping to $191D.

Call $1916 and set border and background black. When $145D is nonzero, change VIC display and bank settings and enable the sprites; then pass X=$58, Y=$18 and A=$AA to $1907 and jump to $191D. The captured frame next selects handler $1858.

Call $1916, delay with twelve NOPs, write $18 then $78 to $D011, and set the VIC bank and memory and display registers. Pass X=$8C, Y=$18 and A=$B0 to $1907, then jump to $191D; the captured frame next selects $188C.
Call $1916 and combine $78 with $1903 for $D011. If $1903 is nonzero, pass $18B4 and raster value $B8 to $1907; otherwise pass $18DC and $B7. Both paths jump to $191D.
Call $1916, delay with nine NOPs and combine $10 with $1903 for $D011. If $145E is nonzero call the sound update at $E13A; pass $17D7 and raster value $20 to $1907, then jump to $191D.

Alternate handler selected by $188C when $1903 is zero. Call $1916, delay with three NOPs and a countdown from X=5, then set $D011 from $10 OR $1903. If $145E is nonzero call $E13A; pass $17D7 and raster value $20 to $1907 and jump to $191D.
Write X and Y as the low and high bytes of the next hardware IRQ vector, write A to the raster compare register $D012, acknowledge the raster interrupt, and return.
Save A, X and Y in zero-page bytes $02, $03 and $04, respectively.
Restore A, X and Y from zero-page bytes $02–$04 and return from the interrupt with RTI.

Bitmap bytes for character rows 0 through 2 of the opening-story picture. The VIC reads these bytes in bank 1 during the captured multicolour bitmap band; each row spans 320 bytes. The full reconstructed frame differs from VICE by two pixels.

Bitmap bytes for character rows 3 through 5 of the opening-story picture. The VIC reads these bytes in bank 1 during the captured multicolour bitmap band; each row spans 320 bytes. The full reconstructed frame differs from VICE by two pixels.

Bitmap bytes for character rows 6 through 8 of the opening-story picture. The VIC reads these bytes in bank 1 during the captured multicolour bitmap band; each row spans 320 bytes. The full reconstructed frame differs from VICE by two pixels.

Bitmap bytes for character rows 9 through 11 of the opening-story picture. The VIC reads these bytes in bank 1 during the captured multicolour bitmap band; each row spans 320 bytes. The full reconstructed frame differs from VICE by two pixels.

Bitmap bytes for character rows 12 through 14 of the opening-story picture. The VIC reads these bytes in bank 1 during the captured multicolour bitmap band; each row spans 320 bytes. The full reconstructed frame differs from VICE by two pixels.

Six hundred screen-matrix bytes for the first fifteen rows of the opening-story bitmap. In multicolour bitmap mode each byte supplies two colours for one eight-by-eight cell. The captured frame reads this matrix in VIC bank 1; colour RAM and the background register supply the other colours.
Eighteen space-padded 40-byte rows of story text about the baby carriage incident, followed by a zero byte. The renderer and the zero byte purpose remain open.
Ten space-padded 40-byte rows of story text about Spengler and Stantz investigating the site, followed by a zero byte. The renderer and the zero byte purpose remain open.
Eleven space-padded 40-byte rows of story text about the fake roadworks and the airshaft, including the start prompt, followed by a zero byte. The renderer and the zero byte purpose remain open.

Use A to select a seven-byte record at $EB5C: one accumulator increment and three little-endian pointers. Clear the three $24-byte channel state blocks, initialize their pointers and counters from the selected record, clear SID registers, and enable the channel update flags.
Call the three-voice SID update at $E141, then call the separate routine at $E937 before returning.

If $E12E is nonzero, advance an eight-bit accumulator; on carry call $E3A3 for channel offsets $00, $24 and $48, then call $E43D for all three. For each enabled channel, write its stored frequency, pulse width, envelope and control values to the SID; finally write $E138 to $D418.
Immediate operand of the LDA at $E146. Initialization copies the selected record's first byte here; each enabled sound update adds it to the accumulator stored in the operand at $E14A.

Immediate operand of the ADC at $E149 and the accumulator for the sound update. Initialization writes $FF here; the update stores each sum back. Carry from the addition controls whether it advances the three channel streams.

For the channel selected by X, read a byte from the stream addressed by $E0CB/$E0CC plus $E0CD. A byte with bit 7 set resets the stream offset to $FF and has that bit cleared. Add $E0D3, the global offset at $E464 and $E0E5; use the result to select a little-endian frequency from $E5C2. The continuation at $E464 applies the channel's optional frequency and pulse adjustments and stores the resulting SID values in its state block.

Immediate operand of the ADC at $E463. Initialization clears it; a sound-stream command at $E2C7 replaces it. The same routine then adds the channel byte at $E0E5, looks up a two-byte frequency and applies enabled pitch and pulse-width adjustments before storing the channel's frequency at $E0D6/$E0D7 and pulse width at $E0D8/$E0D9.
Update the shared modulation state, then call each active voice's effect routine according to the three flags at $E12F-$E131.

Update the first voice's timed effect. When its remaining count reaches zero, clear its active flag and envelope registers and set its completion flag. Otherwise count down the effect, periodically reload its frequency and add or subtract its configured frequency step before writing SID voice 1.
Update the second voice's timed effect: clear its flag and envelope on expiry, otherwise count down, reload and step its frequency and write SID voice 2.
Update the third voice's timed effect: clear its flag and envelope on expiry, otherwise count down, reload and step its frequency and write SID voice 3.
Clear the four sound flags at $E12E–$E131, then clear SID registers $D400–$D417. The following entry at $EB34 performs only the register clear.
Shift the four-byte state at $EB58-$EB5B, feeding in a value derived from $EB58 and the incoming carry; return the new byte at $EB58.
